# Unicode 17 URL host processing sources

Runtime code is a pure Dart port of the nontransitional WHATWG path in
[jsdom/tr46 6.0.0](https://github.com/jsdom/tr46/tree/v6.0.0), with the
[RFC 3492 codec from punycode.js 2.3.1](https://github.com/mathiasbynens/punycode.js/tree/v2.3.1).
The original sources and MIT licenses are retained here for review. None of the
JavaScript files execute in the Dart runtime or CI generation step.

Release artifacts (SHA-256):

- https://registry.npmjs.org/tr46/-/tr46-6.0.0.tgz —
  `8737146639e92140a7bf77090b8a09539ec7610b60fcf9a412567cb7280e2881`
- https://registry.npmjs.org/punycode/-/punycode-2.3.1.tgz —
  `e4ce59f9fbac44349abab87279ab658f6b4614916bec5e088ae3be9323e193bb`

The tr46 release's package.json pins Unicode 17.0.0. Its generated mapping
ranges, combining marks, virama, joining and Bidi regular expressions are
translated mechanically into Dart data. The port enables CheckBidi and
CheckJoiners and disables CheckHyphens, UseSTD3ASCIIRules, VerifyDnsLength and
transitional processing; invalid Punycode is rejected. URL forbidden-domain
characters and numeric IPv4 parsing run after domain-to-ASCII, as required by
[WHATWG URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-domain-to-ascii).

NFC uses the exact pure Dart dependency `unorm_dart: 0.3.2`, which documents
Unicode 17.0 in its [changelog](https://pub.dev/packages/unorm_dart/versions/0.3.2/changelog).
Version 0.3.3 changes to Unicode 18, so do not loosen this pin without reviewing
canonical-runtime compatibility. The pub lockfile pins its artifact hash. The
package's MIT license remains applicable to that dependency; attribution is
retained in the dependency's distributed LICENSE.

Generation is deterministic and offline. From the package directory, using the
workspace Dart 3.13 SDK, run `python3 tool/generate_tr46.py`; use `--check` to
verify source hashes and generated bytes. CI checks generation and runs the
checked-in Unicode 17 IDNA and NFC conformance suites. Source updates require
reviewing upstream code, data, licensing and the canonical runtime, not simply
regenerating with the latest dependency.
